title: What if…
lede: Three decisions where the story could have gone differently. The “What if” panels are speculation, labeled as such.

forks.actual: Coleco announced the Adam in June 1983 and spent heavily ahead of sales that never came; it lost $7.4M in 1983 and $79.8M in 1984.[^3][^4]
forks.whatif: Without the Adam, Coleco would probably have gone into the Cabbage Patch boom with most of its 1983 equity of $89.4M intact, rather than $10.5M. It would still have had a console business in a collapsing video game market.

forks.actual: Coleco ended 1985 with $110M of cash, then raised about $160M more in 15-year debentures. Analysts later said it borrowed to expand.[^3][^11]
forks.whatif: Without that new debt, Coleco would have faced the 1986 doll slump with fewer obligations. Whether it could have found another hit is unknowable.

forks.actual: Cabbage Patch Kids and Trivial Pursuit were both licensed; Coleco lost Trivial Pursuit in 1988 and Hasbro had to agree terms with Original Appalachian Artworks to take on the dolls.[^7][^12]
forks.whatif: Owned brands would have been worth more as collateral and in a sale. It might not have changed the falling demand.
